newsitem.title: CANADA: Saskatchewan seeds 65 percent of crop as of Sunday.
newsitem.headline: Saskatchewan seeds 65 percent of crop as of Sunday.

text.p: Saskatchewan farmers seeded 65 percent of 1997 crops as of Sunday compared to 32 percent at the same time last year and ahead of the five-year average of 61 percent, Saskatchewan Agriculture said in its weekly crop report.
"Warm weather and good soil moisture reserves are making for nearly ideal spring planting conditions and seeding is expected to advance in all areas this week," it said.

Seeding operations were more than three quarters done in southern districts with southwest areas more than 95 percent completed. An average 17 mm (0.7 inch) of rain fell with some areas receiging trace amounts and others 65 mm (2.6 inches).

Central Saskatchewan reported 60 percent of the crop was seeded, compared with seven percent last week. West central areas were 85 percent planted while east central regions were 33-40 percent done. An average 13 mm (0.5 inch) of rain fell.
Northern districts were 54 percent seeded, up from 19 percent last week. The northeast was the least advanced at 44 percent of the crop planted. An average 7 mm (0.3 inch) of rain fell.
Top soil moisture was rated excessive on six percent of crop land, 80 percent good and 14 percent fair to poor.
